binders: There exists a real number C.
Universally quantified thereafter: a type Ω equipped with a measurable space, a measure μ on Ω equipped with the structure of a probability measure, and a sequence X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ.
hypotheses: Every coordinate function X_i : Ω → ℝ is measurable.
The extended nonnegative quantity M := sup_i inf{t ∈ ENNReal : t≠0, t≠∞, exp(X_i²/(toReal t)²) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(X_i²/(toReal t)²) dμ ≤ 2} is finite.
conclusions: For μ-almost every ω, sup_i ENNReal.ofReal(|X_i(ω)|/sqrt(1+log(i+1))) is finite.
The real-valued function ω ↦ ENNReal.toReal(sup_i ENNReal.ofReal(|X_i(ω)|/sqrt(1+log(i+1)))) is μ-integrable.
Its integral is at most C times toReal(M).
mathematical_definitions: For each coordinate f, define its scale N(f) as the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero t satisfying measurability of f, integrability of exp(f²/(toReal t)²), and integral at most 2.
Define M := sup_i N(X_i) in ENNReal.
Define S(ω) := sup_i ENNReal.ofReal(|X_i(ω)|/sqrt(1+log(i+1))) and Y(ω) := ENNReal.toReal(S(ω)).
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal constant C>0 such that, on every probability space and for every sequence of measurable real-valued functions whose exponential-square scales have a finite uniform supremum M, the normalized pointwise supremum S(ω)=sup_{i∈ℕ}|X_i(ω)|/sqrt(1+log(i+1)) is finite almost everywhere, its real-valued version is integrable, and ∫ S dμ≤C M, with the displayed equality of notation understood through the ENNReal embeddings and toReal conversions in the formal definitions.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The sequence is indexed by ℕ starting at 0; its first denominator is sqrt(1+log 1)=1.
No independence, centering, identical-distribution, or other probabilistic relation among the X_i is assumed.
The coordinate-scale predicate explicitly excludes t=0 and t=∞ and additionally requires integrability of the exponential function, not merely a finite displayed integral value.

The target does not separately assert that the admissible-scale set for each coordinate is nonempty; it defines the scale directly as an ENNReal infimum. The finite-global-supremum hypothesis constrains the resulting values but is the only explicit global domain condition.

ENNReal.toReal sends ∞ to 0. The global hypothesis M<∞ makes the right-side conversion genuine. Crucially, the newly exposed Filter.Eventually conclusion states S(ω)<∞ almost everywhere, so the integrand's conversion agrees almost everywhere with the actual finite supremum; only a μ-null exceptional set can be collapsed from ∞ to 0.
Integrability and the final integral concern the explicitly defined function ENNReal.toReal∘S. Values on the exceptional null set do not affect the measure-theoretic integral.
The one constant C must work uniformly for every type Ω, measurable structure, probability measure, and measurable sequence satisfying the finite-scale hypothesis.
The proposition gives only existence and positivity of C; it supplies no numerical value or optimality claim.
